In a lengthy interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discussed the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and talked about the company's plans for a tab-less interface. Watch the video below.

Work functionality may soon be seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern posted a trailer for an interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern published the full interview, which covers the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware plans, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern noted OpenAI's earlier decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps and the simultaneous rollout of ChatGPT's new agent mode, Work.

The merged interface has been confusing, especially for users who just want to keep using ChatGPT but can no longer easily find their conversations.

OpenAI has since updated the app to add 'Work' and 'Chat' tabs at the top of the interface, along with a dropdown menu in the left sidebar for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is no longer quite as hard to use, the overall experience is still a bit convoluted.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's characterization that the new interface was "a bit of a mess," and added that it's "a gradual progression" toward the future where the Work tab disappears and its functionality becomes "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also said that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI has seen the results it expected, with Codex users doubling from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was simply a result of stuffing Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman conceded again, but argued that was partly the point:

The full interview is quite interesting and well worth a watch. There's a very Joanna Stern moment where she tries to bring in ChatGPT Voice mid-conversation, and it goes about as smoothly as you'd expect.
